analysis: Examined the base text of ClusterService.swift (lines 1-910), covering the control lock, service lock, link responder, command dispatch, sync, relay and status. The visible patch excerpt is truncated and only the base side is supplied, so the head changes are only partly visible: a new private updateWaitLine state (head 107-108), a status field value.pairUpdate read from ClusterServiceAgent.updateProgressPath(serviceDirectory: store.paths.directory) (head 943), and in checkForUpdate a new ClusterOnboardingUpdate.oneBuild(pinned:current:) guard (head 974-984) that returns early with a one-time say() line while the two Macs run different builds. Security-relevant reading: (1) The oneBuild guard only defers re-planning and does not widen authorization. It does not touch the pairing edge secret, the followsPeer checks, or the claim-supersede logic in command(). A stalled wait is an availability concern rather than a confidentiality one, and a peer that reports a different runtime binary hash could only delay re-planning. That peer is already the authenticated paired Mac, and the cluster code sits outside the A-001 consumer-prompt path covered by the retained threat entries. (2) ClusterPairUpdate.readProgress reads a file from the service directory (owner-only private mode) and is published in the status reply sent to the paired Mac. I could not see its contents or how it is parsed, so what it discloses (paths, versions, error text) and whether parsing is bounded are unverified. The updateWaitLine string contains only model name and Mac labels. (3) Unchanged surrounding code that depends on the link responder, ClusterMemberCacheControl, and the model provision responder was not modified in the visible ranges. I did not see the head text for lines 989 or the rest of the 974-984 hunk, so remaining questions concern the readProgress implementation and the oneBuild semantics, which live in other files. I do not find a concrete regression in what was supplied and mark deeper review as modest uncertainty.
